summary: 18.5 contradicts itself on the battery's round field. 'Three things are called a battery' says "the event's `round` field is the orchestrator's label and is not checked". 'A valid battery, stated once' (G1-4, S2.1) makes validity require "its `round` follows the scope's earlier batteries (1, 2, 3 in order)". A reader cannot tell whether round ordering is a validity condition.

18.5 and 18.7 disagree on a closing review recorded by the closer (D3-1). 18.5 'A review that is not independent' says "a valid closing review recorded by the closer itself blocks the close". 18.7 (Closure, round 3) says "a closing review recorded by the closer does not count, whatever the configuration names as reviewers". The two differ when other valid reviews of the step exist: one refuses the close, the other only ignores that review.

18.4 step (3) says "Nothing is copied back from a failed run". Step (4) says the copy-back happens inside the frozen integrity window, so a copied-back tracked file outside the claimed task's files "still fails the run (exit 99, ... INTEGRITY line)". The section does not say whether the files already copied back are undone when the integrity window then fails the run, so the real tree's state after such a failure, and what `copiedBack` means for a failed run, cannot be reconstructed.

18.3 rests the MCP control on "server role must equal the caller's agent_type". 18.3 also states that a call without agent_type is the main session's (the orchestrator), but never says what the hook does when the main session calls another role's role-locked server (for example a reviewer's). 'Without the mode, the orchestrator cannot record a closing review under a reviewer role through a command the hook can read' covers commands only. So whether the orchestrator can record a closing review as a reviewer over MCP, and hence what closure independence (18.3, 18.5) actually rests on, is not stated.

18.5 GF-CLOSE-6 does not say what happens after an acceptance. 'closed is closed' refuses later dispatches, reviews, resolutions and batteries only "after `gf.slice.closed`". Acceptance leaves the scope "unclosed, its findings stay open". The section does not say whether an accepted scope may still receive dispatches, reviews, resolutions or batteries, or be closed later. It also does not say whether the audit's replay of GF-CLOSE-6 judges an acceptance at its event or against findings raised after it, which would make the acceptance's list no longer hold every open finding.

18.0 "R2 attack scope is limited to this model; findings outside it are recorded as limits, not fixed (L-GF-39)" names no mechanism, and the stated rules leave none for serious findings. A critique finding is of kind defect, and GF-CLOSE-2 refuses to defer "a blocking finding and a major defect". GF-CLOSE-6 refuses any blocking finding. So an out-of-model blocking or major defect can only be fixed or withdrawn, which contradicts "not fixed", or it leaves the scope unclosable. "R2" is also not defined in section 18; 18.5 names the steps comprehension, critique and readiness.

18.4 step (1) excludes the project's `.eccode/` from the real-tree hash because "the frozen record window covers it", and 18.7 repeats this. But 18.1 describes that window only as putting back "a change through the record's absolute path". 18.5 lists the working record as specific paths, and its 'Clean tree' places the guard configurations inside `.eccode/` as well. The section does not say whether the window covers all of `.eccode/` (guard configs, `artifacts/`, other groups' `drafts/`), and for a run's absolute-path write those paths have no other run-time check.

18.0 says deliberate tampering with git internals "is detected by content-hash comparison at integration (by the audit's GF-FRZ-2 and GF-CONF-1 now ...)". Per 18.1, GF-FRZ-2 compares only the sealed contract bytes and GF-CONF-1 only the three guard configs. The claim as worded gives no basis for detecting, now, git-internal tampering that touches any other file.

"managed path" is never defined in section 18, although rules depend on it. 18.0 has "on the managed path (the runner is a managed-path tool)"; 18.3 has the Where column "managed" and the "managed-path preflight"/"regime"; GF-RUN-1 says the preflight's managed-path regime "requires" the wiring; GF-CLOSE-6 has "a prevention rule (a rule enforced on the managed path)". F0 only reports the regime. It is not stated which conditions make up the managed path, or what "requires" means for a report that only warns.

18.4 'Pinned forms': "A path argument is inside the project" does not say whether a path argument may be absolute, or how an absolute path into the real project relates to the copy. If allowed, a read form would read the real tree and a writing form (`ruff format <abs path>`) would write it directly, outside the copy's prevention.

18.4 "Writing forms are for group roles only" uses "writing forms" without defining them. Only the 'ruff, writing' row is labelled writing, while the table's Writes column shows other forms that write too (alembic upgrade/revision: the database and `migrations/`; playwright: result folders; pytest `--cov`). Which forms a role in no group may run is therefore not stated.

18.1 Drafts row: "group roles write only `.eccode/drafts/<group>/**`". Clarifications: G1 artifacts under `.eccode/artifacts/` are "written by the document authors, `delivery-lead` included", and `contracts/` is "drafted by the document authors ... before the seal", while GF-FRZ-1 refuses contract writes by a non-api group role. The section does not say whether the document authors (delivery-lead among them) are group roles, or whether the Drafts and GF-FRZ-1 restrictions apply before the seal, so these statements may conflict.

18.3: under `ECCODE_SEQUENTIAL_ROLES=1` "the main session may act as any role". It is not said whether the main session is still asked before acting as `user`. 18.5 GF-CLOSE-6 rests the owner-only acceptance on "asks the person before the main session runs it (18.3)" but does not carry over 18.3's statement that a command hiding the CLI from the text (script file, `node -e`) escapes the check. The case is stated for closing reviews (L-GF-33) but not for `--actor user` acceptances.

Limit id L-GF-26 is cited for two different residuals. In 18.5 it covers the battery's test command, base and mutant count ("are the orchestrator's choice ... (L-GF-26)"). In 18.6 it covers a hidden counter reset ("A reset that later use hides behind a larger `end` is not detectable (L-GF-26)"). From section 18 alone it cannot be told whether this is one limit or a mis-citation.

18.5 'Records, stated precisely': "A readiness review needs at least one citation; a `path:line` resolves when ...; an `ev:<id>` resolves when ...". It does not say whether every citation must resolve or only one, or whether a review with an unresolved citation is refused when recorded or merely invalid at close.

18.0 frames the threat as "project code that an agent runs (a test, a migration, a formatter)". Its 'Outside the model' list (restore within a run, writes outside the project, forged appends) omits project code that the orchestrator, a reviewer role or a role in no group runs in its own shell on the real tree. 18.4 keeps that shell ("keep the shell they have, with the hook's text-level checks"). It is therefore unclear whether such writes are in or out of the threat model and of R2's attack scope.
